title: Rising LFP feedstock prices could bolster recycling economics
gist: Hunan Yuneng is raising prices on its entire LFP cathode active material range by a flat RMB2,000/t (USD296/t) from 1 August 2026, blaming geopolitical and supply-chain disruption to sulphur, phosphoric acid and iron sulphate plus demand exceeding capacity. Benchmark argues the squeeze re-rates the neglected iron-phosphate fraction of LFP scrap and improves recycling economics. The article body is truncated by a registration wall.

insights.claim: Hunan Yuneng is raising prices on all of its lithium iron phosphate products by a flat RMB2,000 per tonne (USD296/t) effective 1 August, an across-the-board increase rather than a grade-specific one.
insights.speaker: Benchmark Team
insights.so_what: A flat per-tonne hike from the largest-profile LFP CAM supplier sets a visible floor for cathode pricing that cell makers and EV OEMs will have to absorb or pass through.
insights.quote: Hunan Yuneng will raise prices for all lithium iron phosphate products by a flat rate of RMB2,000/t (USD296/t) from 1 August
insights.locator: In July, Hunan Yuneng announced a price increase

insights.claim: The stated drivers of the LFP cathode price increase are cost inflation in sulphur, phosphoric acid and iron sulphate attributed to global geopolitical fluctuations and supply chain disruptions.
insights.speaker: Benchmark Team
insights.so_what: The battery cost story has shifted from lithium to the phosphate/sulphur chemical chain — watch industrial-chemical suppliers of phosphoric acid and sulphur as an under-followed battery input trade.
insights.quote: citing "global geopolitical fluctuations and supply chain disruptions" affecting sulphur, phosphoric acid, and iron sulphate
insights.locator: In July, Hunan Yuneng announced a price increase

insights.claim: Hunan Yuneng cites strong demand exceeding available capacity as a co-driver of its price increase, indicating LFP cathode supply is currently tight rather than in the glut normally assumed for Chinese battery materials capacity.
insights.speaker: Benchmark Team
insights.so_what: Tight LFP CAM capacity cuts against the consensus overcapacity narrative in Chinese battery materials and argues for pricing power at incumbent cathode makers.
insights.quote: citing higher upstream raw material costs and strong demand exceeding available capacity

insights.claim: Rising LFP feedstock prices could be a boon for the LFP recycling market by making the full basket of recoverable materials in LFP scrap economically worth capturing.
insights.speaker: Benchmark Team
insights.so_what: Battery recyclers' margins are levered to cathode input costs, not just to lithium price — an input-cost spike is a direct recycler-margin catalyst.
insights.quote: This could represent a boon for the LFP recycling market.

insights.claim: LFP recycling has traditionally prioritised recovering lithium carbonate because of its higher value, while recovery of iron phosphate received less attention — a hierarchy the current price surge challenges.
insights.speaker: Benchmark Team
insights.so_what: Recyclers with process flowsheets that recover iron phosphate as well as lithium gain relative value; pure lithium-focused recovery is now leaving revenue on the table.
insights.quote: Traditionally, this market has prioritised lithium carbonate among the recoverable materials due to its higher value, while recovery of iron phosphate has received less attention.
